item.title: Future building electricity demand peaks
item.content:encoded:
Nature Reviews Earth & Environment, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43017-026-00867-y

An article in PNAS (Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences) examined how the future electricity demand of buildings in the USA might change with climate and technology adoption.

item.title: Crater descent to refresh the magmatic record of Oldoinyo Lengai
item.content:encoded:
Nature Reviews Earth & Environment, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43017-026-00854-3

Oldoinyo Lengai is Earth’s only active volcano erupting carbonatite lavas, which provide insights into deep carbon cycling. However, an eruption in 2007–8 created a 130-m-deep crater that made fresh lava inaccessible. In 2026, field conditions finally enabled a crater descent route to sample fresh lava and reconnect the magmatic record.

item.title: Rapid ice loss events in a warming Arctic
item.content:encoded:
Nature Reviews Earth & Environment, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43017-026-00848-1

The gradual transition of the Arctic sea-ice cover towards a seasonal ice-free state will likely be accelerated by rapid ice loss events (RILEs). This Review explores the mechanisms and impacts of RILEs and their projected role in Arctic sea-ice loss.
